images.caption: Only one temple was restored from this group. Its entrance faces west  (photo right; the view is from the north). The temple's three-tiered roof carries stupika finials and triangular pediments; the diamond pattern on the first course of the roof is also found on batik. A kala-makara arch frames the niches. There is a cornice, curved like a bow, above the kala.

images.caption:
Gedong Songo III.
This group of three temples includes a Nandi temple in the lower right, facing as usual its corresponding Shiva temple. The remaining temple is unpaired. The larger temple (photo center) carries a complete, although understandably rather worn, set of exterior sculptures in relief.
images.alt:
Gedong Songo III.

images.filename: Larger Shiva Temple, Gedong Songo III, 1210.jpg
images.caption: Besides its exterior reliefs, the larger temple once carried a kala-makara arch around its entrance door, and also a makara staircase. The temple's west (entrance) and north sides are seen here. Its elaborate roof decorations include a triangular pediment, above the entrance; stupika finials; and rather large, free-standing antefixes at the centers of the eaves.
images.alt: Besides its exterior reliefs, the larger temple once carried a kala-makara arch around its entrance door, and also a makara staircase. The temple's west (entrance) and north sides are seen here. Its elaborate roof decorations include a triangular pediment, above the entrance; stupika finials; and rather large, free-standing antefixes at the centers of the eaves.

images.filename: West Face, Larger Shiva Temple, Gedong Songo III, 1209.jpg
images.caption:
West Face (entrance) of the Larger Shiva Temple, Gedong Songo III.
The temple is entered on the west side, where Nandishvara and Mahakala, the canonical dvarapalas (guardians) of Shiva's temples, 
flank the doorway. Nandishvara, on the left, holds a water pot; Mahakala, on the right, holds a club. A nearly-erased kala on the lintel, and worn makara heads beneath the niches, are almost all that remains of the kala-makara arch that originally framed the doorway.

images.filename: Ganesha, Larger Shiva Temple, Gedong Songo III, 1206.jpg
images.caption:
Ganesha. Larger Shiva Temple, Gedong Songo III
The temple's east niche shelters Ganesha, Shiva's elephant-headed son. He sits with the soles of his feet pressed together; this is his typical asana in Indonesia, although nowhere else in Asia. His fan-shaped ears are also an Indonesian variant. In his crown he bears Shiva's crescent moon (Chandra), reinforcing his connection to his father.

images.caption: Appropriately enough for a Shiva temple, this roof is covered in lingas. The surrounding shrines, whose bases are visible in this photograph, could not be restored, because too many of their stones are missing.

images.caption: The single restored temple in Group V has a roof that is decorated with lingas, like the temple from Group IV. Its entrance faces west, and is framed by the remains of a kala-makara arch. Nandishvara and Mahakala guardians, like those in Group III, would originally have occupied the flanking niches.

images.caption:
This is a JPEG format plan and architectural drawing of a historic Indian temple or monument. An alternate SVG format (scalable vector graphics) version of this file – for web graphics, design studies, print, dynamic and interactive applications – has also been uploaded to wikimedia commons.
The drawing:

Gedong Songo complex of temples is located on the hillside of Mountain Ungaran. It has nine temples grouped in five Gedong (lit. complex of temples). Gedong-1 and Gedong-2 are on the eastern side of the hill, Gedong-3 and Gedong-4 to the north side, and Gedong-5 to the west of the hill. This is a historic volcanic region of central Java, and these temples are built from the volcanic rocks cut and carved into reliefs. These are Shiva temples.
This is the floor plan of one of the nine Gedong Songo temples.
The temple's architectural plan follows the square and circle principle found in historic Sanskrit texts.
For further information, see N.J. Krom and F.D.K. Bosch (1914-1915), Inventarisatie der Hindoe-oudheden op den grondslag; R.D.M. Verbeek (1915), Oudheden van Java samengesteld op het Oudheidkundig Bureau; N.J. Krom (1923), Inleiding tot de Hindoe-Javaansche Kunst. For archival photos, see the collection of Oudheidkundige Dienst.

images.filename: Durga Mahishasuramardini, Larger Shiva Temple, Gedong Songo III, 1208.jpg
images.caption:
Durga Mahishasuramardini. Larger Shiva Temple, Gedong Songo III.
A very worn Durga, in the act of killing the buffalo demon Mahisha, decorates the temple's north exterior niche. The goddess's multiple arms are the most prominent attributes that still remain on the sculpture.
images.alt:
Durga Mahishasuramardini. Larger Shiva Temple, Gedong Songo III.
A very worn Durga, in the act of killing the buffalo demon Mahisha, decorates the temple's north exterior niche. The goddess's multiple arms are the most prominent attributes that still remain on the sculpture.

images.filename: Agastya, Larger Shiva Temple, Gedong Songo III, 1207.jpg
images.caption:
Larger Shiva Temple, Gedong Songo III.
The south niche is occupied by Agastya, a legendary missionary of Shiva in India who eventually became regarded as an avatar of the god himself. The potbellied and bearded guru stands on a lotus throne. His arms and the attributes they once carried are broken off, but a clear outline of Shiva's trident is visible at the statue's proper left side.

images.filename: Gunung Prau, Dieng, Wonosobo, Jawa Tengah, 04072015.jpg
images.caption:
Gunung prau terletak di tiga kabupaten yaitu kabupaten Wonosobo, kabupaten Kendal, kabupaten Batang. Memiliki ketinggian 2.565 mdpl.
Kenapa disebut prau, karena bentuk gunung ini yang memanjang seperti perahu. Gunung prau memiliki pemandangan yang indah dan sunrise terbaik yang muncul sekitar bulan desember-januari.
